- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price dropping after peak), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast is trending, apply a 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid erratic swings.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, assume sentiment is bullish and adjust next forecast upward by 1–3% to reflect momentum.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by >3% over 10+ days, check for sentiment lag — if sentiment is rising, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
